why.B1.1: Hypoplastic Left Heart Syndrome is a strong candidate due to the single S2, systolic ejection murmur, and enlarged cardiac silhouette, but it is less specific for the increased pulmonary vasculature.
why.B2.3: Patent ductus arteriosus is a possible explanation for the enlarged cardiac silhouette and increased pulmonary vasculature, but the single S2 and systolic ejection murmur are less typical for this condition.
why.B4.4: Truncus Arteriosus best explains the single S2, systolic ejection murmur, and enlarged cardiac silhouette with increased pulmonary vasculature due to the common arterial trunk and excessive blood flow to the lungs.

fact_rationales.F15: Enlarged cardiac silhouette with increased pulmonary vasculature is highly suggestive of Hypoplastic Left Heart Syndrome, which often presents with increased pulmonary blood flow and cardiomegaly.

3f16cbb4cad2682a6bb965ebe724a9a105bf0a06.why: selected facts provide contrast between Truncus Arteriosus and Tricuspid Atresia

fact_rationales.F12: A single S2 and systolic ejection murmur can be associated with various cardiac defects, but the presence of a systolic ejection murmur is more typical of ventricular septal defects.
fact_rationales.F15: An enlarged cardiac silhouette with increased pulmonary vasculature is more commonly seen in conditions with a left-to-right shunt, such as patent ductus arteriosus, but can also be seen in other defects like ventricular septal defects.

fact_rationales.F12: Single S2 and systolic ejection murmur are more typical of truncus arteriosus due to the common arterial trunk, whereas tricuspid atresia would more likely present with different auscultation findings due to the absence of the tricuspid valve.
fact_rationales.F15: Enlarged cardiac silhouette with increased pulmonary vasculature is highly suggestive of truncus arteriosus due to the excessive blood flow to the lungs, whereas tricuspid atresia might show different imaging characteristics due to the underdevelopment of the right ventricle and the presence of atrial septal defect or patent foramen ovale.
